Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:47: Behold, you have learned that whenever the Holy One, blessed be He, gives greatness to the righteous, they lower themselves - and therefore Israel are compared to a vine, as it is said (Psalms 80:9), "You have moved a vine out of Egypt" - just as this vine, every cluster greater than its fellow is lower than its fellow, so with Israel, whoever is greater must be more humble than his fellow (Yalkut, part 1, remez 146). Similarly, an ordinary person bows in prayer four times - at the beginning and end of the Avot blessing, and at the beginning and end of the Hoda'ah blessing - but the High Priest bows at every single blessing, and the king bows at the beginning of every single blessing and at its end (Berachot 34a-b) - to teach you that whoever is greater than his fellow must be more humble.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:48: And when a person makes himself small, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him up, as it is said (I Samuel 2:8), "He raises the poor from the dust," and so on, "and He makes them inherit a throne of glory." Up to here, from Sefer Menorat HaMaor by Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, although I have shortened his words in some places, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:49: And so we find several Tannaim and Amoraim in the Gemara who were praised for humility. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, in Bava Metzia (84b), said of Rabbi Elazar, whom Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel considered equal to Rabbi his own son - Rabbi's mind grew troubled by this - he [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] came and said to him, my son, let it not trouble you: he is a lion, son of a lion, while you are a lion, son of a fox. And it says shortly after (85a), rather, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was humble.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:50: And further, several places in the Gemara we find [Sages] praised for the attribute of humility. Hillel the Elder is well known, from what they said of him in Tractate Shabbat (30b); and so Rabbi Frida, in Eruvin (54b), who repeated the halachah to his student four hundred times and was not exacting; Bava ben Buta, in Nedarim, chapter "Rabbi Eliezer" (66b) - see there. And further, in Sotah, chapter "Elu Ne'emarin" (40a): Rabbi Abahu said, at first I used to say, I am humble, and so on - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:51: And with this this chapter concludes, and this Gate concludes:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:52: Blessed be the LORD forever, Amen and Amen.
